amendments.rule: Reordered or discontinuous target tokens may occupy one unit when they realize one source item. Do not absorb unrelated intervening words into that unit. **Where English repeats one source function word because its scope is distributed across coordinated or emphatically repeated phrases or clauses, every English occurrence belongs to that source morpheme's one possibly discontinuous unit.** `מִן` in `מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים וְהוֹשֵׁעַ` → *from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging* takes both occurrences of *from*, while the waw takes only *and*; `בִּי אֲנִי` → *upon me ... upon me* gives both occurrences of *upon* to the single preposition while the suffix and explicit pronoun take their respective *me*. The repeated English word is neither `added` nor reassigned to a neighboring source item merely to make the units contiguous. **An explicit personal pronoun is read the same way where the ASV resumes it in a later clause of the same verse.** Where a following verbless clause writes no subject of its own and the ASV supplies the subject pronoun that an explicit `הוּא`, `הֵמָּה`, `אֲנִי` or the like standing earlier in the verse denotes, both occurrences belong to that pronoun's one discontinuous unit, exactly as rule 18 gives both pronouns of a twice-rendered suffix to the suffix and rule 20 gives both halves of an identifying formula to its one `הוּא`: `הֵמָּה סֹחֲרֵי יָדֵךְ ... בָּם סֹחֲרָיִךְ` → *they were the merchants of thy hand ... in these were* ***they*** *thy merchants* gives both *they*s to the one `הֵמָּה`, headed on the first. Such a pronoun is not `added`, and it does not join the predicate's unit: rule 20 hands the predicate the construction's copula and, in a presentative clause, its dummy *there*, and a referential pronoun is neither, so the clause's supplied *were* goes to the predicate while the pronoun goes to the morpheme that denotes it. This governs a clause with no subject of its own: where a finite verb stands in the resumed clause it takes the English subject pronoun under rule 17, which is a pronoun realizing that verb's own person and number. **And where the Hebrew stands the pronoun is not part of the condition.** Hebrew postposes an explicit subject pronoun after its predicate and that predicate's adjuncts, often before a coordinated second subject, while English writes a subject before its verb; where the ASV writes the pronoun in both places it has realized one written morpheme twice, and both occurrences are that pronoun's one discontinuous unit, headed on the first English occurrence: `וְהִנֵּה נִצָּב עַל־עֹלָתוֹ הוּא וְכָל־שָׂרֵי מוֹאָב` → *and lo* ***he*** *was standing by his burnt offering,* ***he*** *and all the princes of Moab* gives both *he*s to the one `הוּא`, while `נִצָּב` keeps the *was standing* rule 20 leaves it and the coordinated subject keeps its own English. So read whether one written pronoun is realized twice rather than which side of the resumption it stands on, and do not hand the first occurrence to the predicate to make the units contiguous: rule 17's permission reaches a pronoun realizing a finite verb's own person and number, and a participle or other predicate morpheme in a verbless clause takes only the copula. **An interrogative particle or a negative whose scope covers coordinated clauses is read the same way.** Where the Hebrew writes `הֲ` or `לֹא` once at the head of the first of two coordinated clauses and the ASV rewrites it at the head of the second, every occurrence belongs to that one morpheme's discontinuous unit, headed on the first: `הֲלוֹא מַחֲזֵה־שָׁוְא חֲזִיתֶם וּמִקְסַם כָּזָב אֲמַרְתֶּם` → ***Have*** *ye* ***not*** *seen a false vision, and* ***have*** *ye* ***not*** *spoken a lying divination* gives both *have*s to the `הֲ` and both *not*s to the `לֹא`, while each verb keeps only its own subject pronoun and lexical verb. This is rule 55's reading of a subordinator the ASV rewrites over a coordinated clause, applied to the particle that governs one. The second occurrence is neither `added` under rule 30 nor folded into the second clause's verb under rule 17. But read what is actually written before applying it: where the Hebrew gaps the morpheme in the second line and the ASV writes a single word carrying both the coordination and the negation, rule 35 governs and that word goes to the waw, as `לֹא עֲלִיתֶם ... וַתִּגְדְּרוּ` → *Ye have not gone up ..., neither built up* leaves the *neither* to the waw alone.
amendments.why: NUM.23.6 is a case rule 25's pronoun sentence was written just past: `וְהִנֵּה נִצָּב עַל־עֹלָתוֹ הוּא וְכָל־שָׂרֵי מוֹאָב` → *and lo he was standing by his burnt offering, he and all the princes of Moab* writes the pronoun twice in English for one `הוּא`, but the Hebrew pronoun stands after the predicate rather than earlier than its resumption, and it is postposed inside its own clause rather than resumed in a following one. Read literally, the existing sentence does not reach it, and a verse pass would be pushed to give the first *he* to the participle — which rule 20's own sentence forbids, since a predicate morpheme is present and an explicit subject takes only its own English — or to mark it `added`. The amendment removes the positional restriction and nothing else: it keeps the head on the first English occurrence, keeps the copula with the predicate under rule 20, and repeats rule 17's limit so the widening cannot be read as licensing a subject pronoun on a participle. The chapter's parallel verse corroborates the division from the other side: at NUM.23.17 the same clause writes `הִנּוֹ` and the suffix takes the one *he*, the participle again keeping only *was standing*.

conventions: מִשָּׁם is read by what stands with it. At 23.13 the ASV writes from whence for אֲשֶׁר ... מִשָּׁם, and the relative, the preposition and the resumptive adverb are one unit headed on the relative under rule 22; the bare מִשָּׁם of the same verse and of 23.27 is from thence and splits, from on מִן and thence on שָׁם. The competing reading — from on מִן with אֲשֶׁר and שָׁם fused as whence — is named in the verse note and was not taken.

גַּם ... לֹא rendered by a single Neither or nor (23.25, twice) is one fused unit headed on the negative, discontinuous around the intervening infinitive absolute, on rule 35's reasoning for waw plus a negative: the one English word carries both the additive and the negation. Do not give the word to גַּם and mark לֹא unrepresented.

The chapter's rule 30 fusions and their heads, each a lexical decision a later verse would otherwise re-argue: בָזֶה → here headed on the demonstrative (23.1, 23.29); כַּאֲשֶׁר → as headed on כְּ by rule 23's governing-first-morpheme test (23.2, 23.30); לְבָדָד → alone headed on the noun (23.9); כָּעֵת → Now headed on the noun (23.23); עַל־פְּנֵי → upon headed on the construct noun (23.28); נַפְשִׁי → me headed on the suffix (23.10); and יִישַׁר בְּעֵינֵי → please headed on the verb (23.27), where the rectum הָאֱלֹהִים keeps its own God and its article is unrepresented.

report: Read all 30 verses end to end against the 48 candidate groups, and separately checked the five added units (23.9 that, 23.11 them, 23.15 Jehovah, 23.19 it, 23.20 commandment), which the lemma table cannot see. No cross-verse split found, so patches is empty.

Candidates that look like splits and are not, each licensed by something written. הֲ takes the fronted auxiliary at 23.12 (Must) and 23.19 (Hath) and is unrepresented at 23.26, where the ASV marks the question by inversion alone — rule 17's own division. אֶל is unrepresented only where the ASV writes a bare object (23.4 and 23.16 met Balaam, 23.26 Told thee) and aligned to unto or to everywhere else, rule 40. The dative לְ is unrepresented at 23.1, 23.7, 23.13, 23.27 and 23.29, where the ASV writes only the bare pronoun, and aligned to unto at 23.11, where it writes the preposition.

Two pairs that look asymmetric are decided by whether a morpheme is present, and both verses cite the governing rule: the two whom's of 23.8 (the first clause writes the resumptive suffix, rule 18; the second writes none, so the supplied whom joins the verb under rule 46's headless-relative clause), and the object markers of 23.12 and 23.26 (the suffix of אֹתוֹ is unrepresented at 23.12, where the ASV writes no resumptive word, and takes the second that at 23.26, where it does). The supplied relative at 23.9 is added rather than joined because the antecedent עָם is written — the far side of the same rule 46 boundary.

The parallel verses agree. 23.1/23.29 and 23.2/23.30 are aligned identically; 23.6/23.17 both give was standing to the participle under rule 20 and the subject pronoun to a pronominal morpheme (the explicit הוּא in one, the suffix of הִנּוֹ in the other). The assimilated [הַ] takes every in all four altar clauses and the written the at 23.9; the רֹאשׁ chains agree at 23.9, 23.14 and 23.28; the cognate infinitive absolutes agree at 23.11 and 23.25, while 23.20's non-cognate בָרֵךְ takes the infinitive marker under rule 52 because rule 56 does not reach it; the four supplied objects and the supplied lexical noun are added in every verse that has one, with no verse folding such a word into a neighbouring verb.

The one asymmetry inside a verse is מִשָּׁם at 23.13: fused with אֲשֶׁר as from whence at s014/s017/s018 and split into from and thence at s033/s034 (and at 23.27). The written relative licenses the difference and the verse names the competing reading, so it stands; recorded as a convention so a later reader need not re-open it.

BSB: none of the 21 disagreements is an error. R × 11 and Sh × 6 are the documented convention differences (BSB attaches the dative and purpose lamed, and the paragogic he, to their host phrase or word). The four singletons are ours by rule and by the English: the waw of 23.3 is the surplus of two waws against one written and (rule 42's count), the הֲ of 23.26 has no auxiliary to take, the הָ of הָאֱלֹהִים at 23.27 has no written the, and the archaic connecting suffix of בְּנוֹ צִפֹּר at 23.18 is 3ms and cannot be the vocative thou, which rule 36 gives to the noun.

Returned besides: three conventions, and one amendment widening rule 25 to cover the postposed explicit pronoun of 23.6, where the ASV writes he twice for one written morpheme and rule 25's existing sentence reaches only a pronoun standing earlier than its resumption.
